newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' 1996 agriculture sector up 3.90 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' 1996 agriculture sector up 3.90 pct.

text.p: The Philippines posted a 3.90 percent growth in value terms in the agriculture sector last year, up from a 1.79 percent expansion registered in 1995, the Department of Agriculture said on Wednesday.

"Compared to the previous year, 1996 saw improved performances of palay (unmilled rice), corn, sugarcane, hogs and chicken. Together, these gainers offset the decline in fisheries output," the department said in a statement.

The value of production in the sector, which includes crops, fisheries, poultry and livestock, went up to 230.479 billion pesos in 1996 as against 221.819 billion pesos the previous year, the department said.
Value of crop production grew by 3.89 percent to 125.239 billion pesos from 120.551 billion pesos in 1995.
Among the major crops, the sugarcane sub-sector posted the highest gain of 33.0 percent both in terms of value and volume, followed by the hemp subsector, 12.81 percent.
Production of unmilled rice, the country's staple food, rose by 4.76 percent to 90.861 billion pesos, while the volume increased by 7.05 percent.
"The major crops recovered from last year's decline and staged a 4.76 percent increment in output this year," the statement added.
However, coconut production posted a decline of 2.04 percent last year both in terms of value and volume.
The livestock industry likewise expanded by 6.40 percent to 30.064 billion pesos from 28.254 billion pesos, despite a decline in volumes by 4.54 percent to 99.24 million tonnes.
The poultry sector posted a 11.32 percent gain in value of production to 31.703 billion pesos from 28.481 billion pesos. Volume of production grew by 13.90 percent to 851.81 million tonnes.
The fisheries sector fell by 2.38 percent in terms of value, and 3.58 percent in terms of volume. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
